after._yoast_wpseo_title: FBX File Format: What It Stores, Uses & Limitations
after._yoast_wpseo_metadesc: Learn what an FBX file stores, how it is used for 3D models and animation, and what to check when transferring assets between applications.

edit.old:
The FBX (Filmbox) file format is among the many file formats used in 3D modeling and graphic design software. Initially developed by Kaydara in 1996, FBX is now owned by Autodesk.

At present, the FBX format remains proprietary, accessible only through software development kits (SDKs) compatible with this file format. An SDK enables a program to correctly interpret the file, and it can be obtained based on C++ in Autodesk or Python in Blender.

In this article, we delve into the FBX file format, exploring its capabilities and comparing it with other file types. We'll also examine its applications in Computer-Aided Design (CAD) systems and 3D printing.
edit.text:
FBX is a 3D file format used to exchange models and scene data between applications. An .fbx file can contain geometry, materials, animation, cameras and lights, making it useful for rendering, animation and game development.

The result of an FBX transfer depends on the exporting and importing applications, the file version and the selected settings. Geometry may transfer successfully while materials, texture connections or animation require adjustment in the destination software.

This guide explains what FBX files can store, where the format is useful, and its main compatibility limits. It also covers considerations when converting a model for 3D printing.
